text.en: A call for Swaraj, or absolute self-rule free from foreign control, said that every nation has the right to live its own life by its own energies. How did India reach that goal?

After the revolt of 1857 the British Crown took direct control of India in 1858.
The Indian National Congress was founded in Bombay in 1885 to voice Indian demands.
In 1905 the partition of Bengal triggered the Swadeshi and boycott movements, and the partition was annulled in 1911.
In 1906 the Congress endorsed Swaraj and the All-India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka.
Gandhi returned from South Africa in 1915, and led satyagraha in Champaran from 1917 and then the Non-Cooperation Movement of 1920–22.
In 1927–28 the Simon Commission was boycotted, and in 1929 the Lahore session of the Congress demanded Purna Swaraj, complete independence.
In 1930 the Civil Disobedience Movement began with the Dandi Salt March, where thousands broke the salt law.
The Government of India Act 1935 introduced provincial autonomy, and in 1942 the Cripps Mission failed and the Quit India Movement was launched.
Subhas Chandra Bose escaped British authority in 1941 and led the Indian National Army, and the INA trials and the 1946 Navy Mutiny weakened British control.
After the Cabinet Mission of 1946, India became independent on 15 August 1947, but the country was also partitioned.
